initiatives.name: eDynamic Learning Acquisition for Early Careers
initiatives.summary: Pearson completed the acquisition of eDynamic Holdings LP (eDynamic Learning), a leading Career and Technical Education (CTE) curriculum solutions provider, to strengthen its Early Careers strategy and digital CTE leadership. The deal was board-reviewed and seen as a key step in a medium-term growth vector.

evidence.title: Acquisition of eDynamic Holdings LP (eDL)
evidence.summary: In 2025, Pearson acquired 100% of eDynamic Holdings LP (eDL). The Audit Committee reviewed the acquisition accounting, including valuation of intangibles and goodwill recognition, with the accounting remaining provisional as of year-end.
evidence.quote: In 2025, Pearson acquired 100% of eDynamic Holdings LP (eDL).

evidence.title: Strategic focus on Early Careers and Enterprise Skilling
evidence.summary: Pearson identified Early Careers and Enterprise Skilling as strategic growth engines, embracing a 'learning to learn' lifelong model instead of the traditional 'learning to earn' model, backed by the eDynamic Learning acquisition and enterprise partnerships.
evidence.quote: That’s why we’ve identified Early Careers and Enterprise Skilling as strategic growth engines. These are not just commercial opportunities; they’re areas where Pearson can make a real societal impact.

evidence.title: Acquisition of eDynamic Learning for Early Careers
evidence.summary: Pearson completed the acquisition of eDynamic Holdings LP (eDynamic Learning), a leading Career and Technical Education (CTE) curriculum solutions provider, to strengthen its Early Careers strategy and digital CTE leadership. The deal was board-reviewed and seen as a key step in a medium-term growth vector.
evidence.quote: On 24 July 2025, the Group completed the acquisition of 100% of eDynamic Holdings LP (‘eDynamic Learning’), a leading Career and Technical Education (CTE) curriculum solutions provider for cash consideration of £168m.

initiatives.name: AI Centre for Enablement and Product Launches
initiatives.summary: Pearson established an AI Centre for Enablement to unify AI standards, tools and expertise across the organization, enabling responsible and scalable deployment of AI solutions and accelerating the shift from experimentation to operational scale.

evidence.title: AI Centre for Enablement (C4E) established
evidence.summary: Pearson established an AI Centre for Enablement to unify AI standards, tools and expertise across the organization, enabling responsible and scalable deployment of AI solutions and accelerating the shift from experimentation to operational scale.
evidence.quote: We established our AI Centre for Enablement (C4E) to unify standards, tools and expertise, enabling the responsible and scalable deployment of AI solutions. This operating model has accelerated our shift from experimentation to operational scale, highlighted by launches such as Communication Coach in Microsoft Teams and the Exam Prep feature in Study Prep.

evidence.title: Communication Coach co-developed with Microsoft
evidence.summary: Pearson launched Communication Coach, co-developed with Microsoft and the Enterprise Learning & Skills business unit, aligned with Pearson's Global Scale of English, to improve communication skills for native and non-native English speakers.
evidence.quote: We advanced our offering with the launch of the PTE Express Test and launched Communication Coach, which was co‑developed with Microsoft and in collaboration with our Enterprise Learning & Skills business unit, to improve the communication ability of both native and non‑native English speakers.

evidence.title: AI-enabled product launches across business units
evidence.summary: Pearson launched multiple AI-powered products including Revibe (AI-enabled wearable with Samsung), GCSE Exam Practice Assistant, 'Go Deeper' AI study tool functionality, and Communication Coach co-developed with Microsoft, to enhance learning outcomes and personalization.
evidence.quote: We also launched Revibe, an AI-enabled wearable powered by Samsung Electronics to support focus and self-regulation. In UK & International Qualifications, we introduced the GCSE Exam Practice Assistant – an AI-powered tool for personalised revision.

initiatives.name: Organisational Restructuring and Career Architecture
initiatives.summary: Pearson merged several teams into a dedicated Revenue Operations unit to standardize sales processes, strengthen pipeline management, and unify data sources, streamlining the organization and bringing teams closer to customers.

evidence.title: Operational simplification via Revenue Operations unit
evidence.summary: Pearson merged several teams into a dedicated Revenue Operations unit to standardize sales processes, strengthen pipeline management, and unify data sources, streamlining the organization and bringing teams closer to customers.
evidence.quote: We merged several teams into a dedicated Revenue Operations unit to standardise sales processes, strengthen pipeline management and unify data sources – delivering clearer, more actionable insights – while launching the next phase of the Pearson Promise to reinforce our high-performance culture and streamline the organisation.

evidence.title: Career Architecture simplification from 1,600 to 140 roles
evidence.summary: Pearson implemented a new Career Architecture that dramatically simplified its organizational role structure from 1,600 to 140 roles, introducing two career tracks and standardized role scope and seniority tiers.
evidence.quote: We simplified our structure from 1,600 to 140 roles, introduced two career tracks (‘Management’ and ‘Expert’), and standardised our approach to role scope and seniority through a new tier structure.

evidence.title: Product operating model rollout and unified architecture
evidence.summary: Pearson accelerated a shift to customer-centricity by rolling out a product operating model organisation-wide, improving product governance and aligning the company to a unified technology architecture.
evidence.quote: We accelerated the shift to true customer-centricity and rolled out our product operating model organisation-wide, delivering significant improvements in product governance and aligning Pearson to a unified architecture.

initiatives.name: Platform Convergence and Legacy Asset Consolidation
initiatives.summary: Pearson recorded an £87 million non-cash, one-off impairment of legacy product development assets as a result of strategic courseware platform convergence, reflecting consolidation of technology platforms.

evidence.title: £87m non-cash impairment from platform convergence
evidence.summary: Pearson recorded an £87 million non-cash, one-off impairment of legacy product development assets as a result of strategic courseware platform convergence, reflecting consolidation of technology platforms.
evidence.quote: The reported operating profit of £507m in 2025 compares to an operating profit of £541m in 2024 due primarily to unfavourable FX movements, inflation and an £87m non-cash, one-off impairment of legacy product development assets arising from strategic platform convergence.

initiatives.name: Copp Clark Higher Education Disposal
initiatives.summary: Pearson disposed of Copp Clark, a business within its Higher Education division, generating a gain on disposal. This is part of ongoing portfolio optimization within Higher Education.

evidence.title: Disposal of Copp Clark business
evidence.summary: Pearson disposed of Copp Clark, a business within its Higher Education division, generating a gain on disposal. This is part of ongoing portfolio optimization within Higher Education.
evidence.quote: The Group disposed of Copp Clark in 2025 for consideration of £9m, resulting in a gain on disposal of £8m, which has been recorded within other net gains and losses.

initiatives.name: GHG Emissions Reduction Against 2018 Baseline
initiatives.summary: Pearson achieved a 44% reduction in GHG emissions (location-based methodology) against its 2018 baseline, driven by shifting suppliers to lower-emitting categories, increased in-market printing, and reduced physical footprint and energy consumption.

evidence.title: 44% GHG emissions reduction achieved against 2018 baseline
evidence.summary: Pearson achieved a 44% reduction in GHG emissions (location-based methodology) against its 2018 baseline, driven by shifting suppliers to lower-emitting categories, increased in-market printing, and reduced physical footprint and energy consumption.
evidence.quote: Achieved an overall reduction of 44% in GHG emissions against our 2018 baseline (location-based methodology)... Decreased our operational energy consumption by 15% from 2024.

initiatives.name: US and Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Termination

initiatives.name: Employee AI Upskilling and Copilot Rollout

evidence.title: AI upskilling and Microsoft Copilot training rollout
evidence.summary: Pearson rolled out Microsoft Copilot access across employees, delivered 140 live training sessions attended by over 4,700 employees, resulting in a 25% increase in Copilot interactions, as part of broader AI literacy investment.
evidence.quote: We delivered 140 live training sessions on Microsoft Copilot in 2025, with 4,722 employees attending a session live. These efforts resulted in a 25% increase in Copilot interactions compared to the number of interactions prior to the training.

initiatives.name: Career Navigation System and Learning Hub
initiatives.summary: Pearson launched the Career Navigation System (CNS), a digital-first personalized platform to build skills and empower career ownership, including the Learning Hub powered by Degreed offering over 800 learning pathways, with employees completing over 23,500 hours of learning since March 2025.

evidence.quote: Employees have completed 23,521 hours of learning and 376,352 microlearning items since March 2025... The integrated Learning Hub, which is powered by Degreed, provides seamless access to career guidance and over 800 learning pathways.

initiatives.name: Share Buyback Programme (Second Tranche)

evidence.title: £350m share buyback programme (second tranche)

evidence.quote: On 21 January 2026, a further £350m share buyback programme was announced. The programme commenced on 21 January 2026.
